Full career trajectory(archival):

- 2001: Began at Goldman Sachs as an analyst, focusing on M&A modeling and surviving the dot-com crash — foundational experience in financial modeling and market volatility.
- 2004: Moved to Morgan Stanley as an associate, gaining early exposure to tech deals during the rise of social media platforms — developed deep understanding of digital-era valuation and growth dynamics.
- At age 31: Promoted to Vice President, leading several landmark transactions that defined the early 2010s tech investment landscape.
- 2015: Joined Legend Investments as Managing Director — marked a pivotal shift toward global, cross-border, and high-impact strategy.
- First major transaction with Legend: NeuralNet Systems IPO — the firm’s largest tech IPO to date, establishing credibility in high-growth tech investing.

Core belief: In global finance, your network and track record are your currency. Trust is not given — it is earned, one successful deal at a time. This principle underpins every decision, relationship, and strategic initiative.
